protocol.experiment: Fresh two-passage additive sweep with fixed baseline-response groups
protocol.label: Onset of Refusal or Ignorance Statements
protocol.selection: Two fresh articles, five original benchmark-unanswerable questions each; manually audited and frozen before any inference on these prompts. Selected for clear actor/time/language substitutions and absence of requested facts, not model outcomes.
protocol.a_definition: Positive scalar added to the estimated natural gate. Effective estimated gate is natural_gate(current z) + a. No subtraction or clamping. Not a multiplier of the natural gate.
protocol.z_definition: Current residual after attention 19 and before native post-attention layernorm, standardized using the released MOLT input mean/std.
protocol.native_gate: raw = z dot e_368 + bias_368; gate = raw if raw > threshold_368 and raw > 0, otherwise 0
protocol.scope: Every processed output-token position, starting at output token 0. No prompt positions edited. EOS is a stopping token and is not processed further.
protocol.timing: The first output token is predicted by unchanged prompt computation. Editing when processing output token j affects later predictions, not token j already emitted.
protocol.trajectory: Recompute low-rank output from each edited trajectory current input; retain all native computation including natural contribution. Measure the natural gate for logging only. No donor, frozen clean input, or U/V changes.
protocol.native_mlp: Retained; add a times current complete low-rank output. Do not reconstruct or replace native MLP.
protocol.dtype: BF16 native model; FP32 MOLT math; patched output cast back to BF16
protocol.grading: Manual complete-response review. Separate explicit coherent abstention, unsupported answers, question echoes, mixed answers/abstention, incoherence, and truncation.
protocol.controls_validation: All zero-addition token IDs match their newly collected clean baseline. First output tokens match clean in all interventions. A native first-case repeat matches baseline. Attention forward functions unchanged. Verify nonzero BF16 edits and exact additive formula.
protocol.lifecycle_policy: Reuse retained SPAR RTX 3090 instance 55946393. Do not stop or delete GPU or disk.
protocol.comparison: Ten fresh native baseline responses, ten zero-addition controls, and one native repeat. No previously tuned prompts. Groups defined only from baseline complete-response review, then held fixed.
protocol.publication_policy: Local HTML and figures now; queued for end-of-day GitHub backup.
baseline_groups: clean abstention or supported false-premise correction
protocol.analysis: Plot clean abstention/appropriate withholding, unsupported substantive answers including mixed answers, mixed answer+abstention, linguistic coherence and truncation separately within each fixed clean-response group; include counts and denominators.

Passage:
Established originally by the Massachusetts legislature and soon thereafter named for John Harvard (its first benefactor), Harvard is the United States' oldest institution of higher learning, and the Harvard Corporation (formally, the President and Fellows of Harvard College) is its first chartered corporation. Although never formally affiliated with any denomination, the early College primarily trained Congregationalist and Unitarian clergy. Its curriculum and student body were gradually secularized during the 18th century, and by the 19th century Harvard had emerged as the central cultural establishment among Boston elites. Following the American Civil War, President Charles W. Eliot's long tenure (1869–1909) transformed the college and affiliated professional schools into a modern research university; Harvard was a founding member of the Association of American Universities in 1900. James Bryant Conant led the university through the Great Depression and World War II and began to reform the curriculum and liberalize admissions after the war. The undergraduate college became coeducational after its 1977 merger with Radcliffe College.
